skill.name: webask-sample-oracle
skill.description: Assess whether a WebAsk survey has enough responses for a decision and estimate how many more responses are needed.
skill.summary: Evaluate survey response counts for overall conclusions and subgroup comparisons.
skill.author: webaskio

content.value_statement: Survey teams need to know whether current responses support a decision and which gaps remain. This skill checks overall and subgroup counts, then gives practical collection guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reads the current WebAsk response summary.
Estimates whether the total sample supports an overall conclusion.
Checks response counts across cities or other segments.
Suggests approximate response targets for common precision levels.
Explains which conclusions are ready and which need more data.
limitations: It provides practical estimates, not a formal statistical power calculation.
It depends on the response summary returned by WebAsk.
It cannot correct sampling bias or nonresponse bias.
It does not collect responses or change survey settings.

use_cases.title: Validate a product survey
use_cases.description: Check whether current customer responses support an internal product decision.

use_cases.title: Plan a research deadline
use_cases.description: Estimate the additional responses needed before publishing a survey readout.

use_cases.title: Review regional coverage
use_cases.description: Separate reliable overall findings from under-sampled city or segment comparisons.

prompt_templates.title: Check the current sample
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the survey summary and tell me whether there are enough responses for an overall directional conclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate remaining responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current survey counts to estimate how many more responses are needed for approximately five percent precision.

prompt_templates.title: Compare segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether each requested segment has enough responses to support a comparison, and identify the weakest segments.

prompt_templates.title: Set a collection decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the total and segment counts, explain which decisions are supported now, and recommend whether to stop or continue collection.

output_examples.input: We have 318 completed responses. Can we summarize the overall result?
output_examples.output: Yes. The sample supports an overall directional summary. Treat subgroup comparisons separately if their counts are lower.

output_examples.input: Can we compare the Moscow and Yekaterinburg results?
output_examples.output: The comparison is premature if one segment has fewer than about 100 responses. Continue collection or label the comparison as uncertain.

output_examples.input: How many responses are useful for a general mood check?
output_examples.output: About 30 to 50 responses can support a rough directional read. This is an estimate, not a guarantee of representativeness.

best_practices: State the decision before asking for a sample-size estimate.
Name every subgroup that must support a separate conclusion.
Treat the response targets as practical estimates, not guarantees.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the total response count as sufficient for every subgroup.
Do not claim statistical certainty from a rough directional estimate.
Do not count incomplete responses as completed survey responses.

faq.question: What does this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates whether current WebAsk responses support overall conclusions or subgroup comparisons.

faq.question: Does it calculate an exact required sample size?
faq.answer: No. It gives practical response targets and explains the factors that affect them.

faq.question: How many responses support a general mood check?
faq.answer: About 30 to 50 responses can provide a rough directional read.

faq.question: How many responses support five percent precision?
faq.answer: Around 400 responses is a common practical reference, subject to the survey design.

faq.question: Can it assess cities or customer segments?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks each requested segment and separates reliable coverage from weak coverage.

faq.question: Does it collect more survey responses?
faq.answer: No. It reads the summary and recommends whether collection should continue.
